clause.text: 1. Form of Sponsorship. During the term of this Agreement, Tickets shall be MP3.com's exclusive partner/source for sports, entertainment, and travel tickets, and MP3.com shall include a Tickets Portal on the "Music" page and the "Pop," "Rock" and "Alternative" genre pages on the Website. A "Portal" is defined as a web graphic with the dimensions not to exceed 125 x 125 pixels and 20Kb in size. The content of the Portal shall be supplied by Tickets and shall conform with reasonable technical and content specifications supplied by MP3.com.

The retrieved playbook positions do not squarely address this subject matter. The revenue-share position [revenue-share-defined] speaks only to how a revenue or profit share is computed and reported - it requires that the share be 'calculated on net revenue actually received' at the Order Form percentage and be paid quarterly 'together with a statement showing the calculation' - and the clause here creates an exclusivity and portal-placement arrangement rather than a revenue or profit share, so that position does not resolve the clause. The no-minimum-commitment position [no-minimum-commitment] addresses only Customer's freedom from minimum purchase or requirement-share obligations, which is a different concern from the exclusivity and portal obligations imposed here. The governing-law-and-venue, mutual-confidentiality and data-processing positions are silent on exclusivity grants, portal placement, or content-specification approval, so no retrieved position governs these terms. Because the clause is not covered by the playbook but also does not conflict with any retrieved position, the risk is assessed as medium rather than high, and the assessment is limited strictly to what the cited positions actually state.

Overall risk is high due to the penalty-like late fee.

clause.text: 4. Term and Termination. This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall remain in full force and effect until one (1) year subsequent to the Effective Date, provided however, that Tickets may terminate this Agreement for any reason upon thirty (30) days' notice to MP3. com at any time prior to the expiration of sixty (60) days subsequent to the Effective Date. Furthermore, for a thirty (30) day period, beginning thirty (30) days prior to the first anniversary of this Agreement, Tickets shall have the right to renew the Agreement for another year with Sponsor Fees that do not exceed a [***] percent increase over the existing Sponsor Fees. Any payments which have accrued prior to the date of termination shall remain due and payable. Sections 6, 7, and 8 shall survive termination of this agreement.

Any payments which have accrued prior to the date of termination shall remain due and payable. Sections 6, 7, and 8 shall survive termination of this agreement.

reviews.rationale: The termination and renewal mechanics deviate materially from the playbook and are asymmetric in favor of Tickets. First, termination for convenience is one-sided and time-limited: only Tickets may terminate 'for any reason upon thirty (30) days' notice' and only during a narrow window ending sixty (60) days after the Effective Date, whereas the playbook contemplates a mutual right ('Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice...'). Second, the renewal is a unilateral option exercisable solely by Tickets, which conflicts with the playbook position that renewal must be opt-in by mutual written agreement and any renewal term must not exceed twelve months. Third, the renewal fee escalation is left as an unknown '[***] percent' figure with no ceiling tied to the playbook cap, and there is no advance notice requirement for the fee, conflicting with the requirement that renewal fee increases be capped (e.g., no more than five percent (5%)) and given on at least sixty (60) days' prior written notice. Together these create high risk: MP3.com is locked into a one-year term with no symmetric exit, faces an unquantified fee escalation at renewal driven by the counterparty, and loses control over whether the agreement renews.

5. Measurement. Upon request, Tickets shall have access to pertinent statistics related to Impressions covering the period of this contract. Tickets agrees to accept MP3.com's measurement of Impressions (the "Count") according to MP3.com's logs and other tracking devices and/or software MP3.com may use, provided however, that Tickets shall have the right to audit MP3.com's records in this regard. If Tickets reasonably disputes the Count pursuant to this Agreement, then Tickets shall have the right to select the independent auditor of its choice to conduct an audit of MP3.com's records (the "Audit"). The Audit will be conducted in such a way so as not to interfere to any material extent with MP3.com's operations. If, for any applicable period, the independent auditor determines that MP3.com overstated the Count by more than five percent (5%), than MP3.com shall pay the cost of the Audit and shall refund Tickets the difference between the amount originally paid and the amount which should have been paid, or MP3.com shall credit the appropriate amount of Impressions to Tickets' account.

reviews.rationale: The clause grants Tickets broad audit rights without the frequency, notice, and confidentiality limitations required by playbook position audit-rights-bounded. The preferred position limits audits to once per 12 months, on 30 days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, at the auditing party's cost, and subject to confidentiality obligations. The fallback position allows no more than twice per 12 months, on 15 days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and subject to confidentiality obligations, with cost shifting only if the audit reveals an underpayment of more than 5%. The clause omits any frequency limit, any prior notice requirement, and any confidentiality obligation for the audit, creating a risk of unfettered audits and potential disclosure of confidential information.

reviews.rationale: The clause is mutual and excludes special, indirect, incidental, and consequential damages, which aligns in part with the playbook position on mutual exclusion of consequential damages. However, it is narrower than the preferred position because it omits punitive damages and lost profits, revenue, goodwill, or data, and it does not include the preferred position’s broader language covering damages 'however caused and regardless of the theory of liability, even if advised of the possibility of such damages.' The exception for claims arising under section 6 is undefined and could be broader than the narrow third-party indemnity exception in the playbook fallback, creating uncertainty about whether certain consequential damages remain recoverable. This results in a medium risk rather than low risk.
